records.text: U.S. sanctions against an International Criminal Court judge made him unable to access banking, buy a ticket, or pay bills.
records.speaker: Bassem Youssef

appearances.snippet: When you sanction a person, ... and they did that for a couple of the judges in the ICC, ... they sanctioned the judge. He's Dutch. ... This guy cannot have access to the bank account, ... cannot have anything like he cannot have money, ... he cannot buy a ticket, ... he cannot pay his own bills. ... He's just like a ghost.

verification.notes: U.S. sanctions on ICC personnel caused frozen or closed bank accounts, canceled cards, blocked booking and travel services, and loss of ordinary payment capabilities. Reporting on Nicolas Guillou and other sanctioned judges directly supports the described everyday consequences.

sources.title: Cut off by their banks and even iced out by Alexa, sanctioned ICC staffers remain resolute
sources.relevance: Documents closed accounts, lost credit cards, travel restrictions, and blocked daily services caused by the sanctions.

sources.title: International Criminal Court-Related Sanctions
sources.relevance: Primary U.S. Treasury source documents the governing sanctions program and blocked-person restrictions.
